..
Issued at 240 PM CST Mon Nov 16 2026

Tuesday through Thursday...

Overall, not any significant changes to the forecast for the
mid-week period...it remains dry, but there is some uncertainty
in that, mainly later in the day Wednesday into Wednesday 
evening. Models are in good agreement showing the generally 
weaker upper level flow currently in place across the area 
making a sharp turn to the south- southwest starting already 
tonight. Through the day on Tuesday, the ridge axis currently 
extending northward through the Plains get increasingly 
pinched/sharper between the slower departing eastern CONUS 
through and a more progressive western system, which moves 
inland from the West Coast by evening. Will be another day with 
gusty southerly winds, as we continue to site between that 
eastern CONUS sfc high and strengthening low pressure over 
portions of WY/CO. Expecting stronger speeds/gusts than today 
with models showing a tighter pressure gradient...gusts around 
40 MPH are certainly not out of the question. Forecast highs 
climb into the mid 50s for most spots...though could be impacted
by potentially slow-to- lift cloud cover. 

As we get into Wednesday, models showing by sunrise, upper level
low pressure is expected to swing northeastward roughly from 
southern NV into the WY/MT border area. Through the daytime 
hours, models show further deepening of this upper low, not 
making a ton of progress east, ending up over the western 
Dakotas by early evening...then continuing its ENE push 
overnight into northern MN. Accompanying this disturbance will 
be a surface frontal boundary...making its main push through the
forecast area during the late afternoon/evening hours. Ahead of
this boundary...expect again gusty south-southwesterly winds 
(potentially gusting again near 40 MPH in spots), eventually 
diminishing to closer to 10-15 MPH by the end of the day. Main 
question as far as precipitation chances go during the mid-week 
period lie in this late day-evening period...as a few models 
continue to show the potential for spotty light precip 
developing near that sfc frontal boundary as it pushes through. 
Not a ton of support...thus the NBM and forecast remains dry, 
but it's not totally out of the question some spotty precip 
develops. Expecting another bump up in highs for Wednesday, with
low-mid 60s forecast.

Forecast remains dry through Thursday...with the area looking to
be sitting between upper level systems...one continuing its 
ENE trek out of MN through Ontario, and the next working its way
inland from the West Coast. Light/potentially variable winds 
start the day, then turn back to the south as sfc low pressure 
starts getting better organized over the Rockies/High Plains 
ahead of this next system. Wednesday's frontal passage isn't a 
notable one...doesn't have a punch of strong NWrly winds nor a 
push of colder air, as highs Thursday are in the upper 50s-mid 
60s for most of the area.

Friday and on...

As far as preciptiation chances go to end the week into the
upcoming weekend...compared to even just a few days ago, 
models had really trended back on the coverage/amounts...and 
most recent models haven't deviated from that. Models showing 
that the brunt of lift with this upper level disturbance largely
tracks north of the forecast area...taking the best 
precipitation chances along. Total QPF through the Friday-
Saturday time frame area remains on the low side...GEFS/ECMWF 
ens probabilities of even just 0.1in or more have dropped down 
into the 10-40 percent range for most of the forecast area, 
those higher probabilities lie mainly north of I-80. Not that 
models had shown a ton of instability building in across the 
area on Friday ahead of the approaching sfc cold front...but 
that too has diminished, forecast currently has no thunder 
mention at all Fri- Sat. Forecast for Sunday is dry.

For temperatures...Friday highs are back in the low-mid 60s
ahead of the cold front, with gusty southerly winds returning 
after a relative break on Thursday. Once the cold front pushes 
through Friday night, highs fall back into the 40s-50s for 
Saturday, with 40s for Sunday.
